historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is negative (buybacks reducing book value, First Data acquisition leverage). EPS CAGRs are distorted upward by share count reduction. Revenue 3yr CAGR of 6.1% selected as primary anchor but capped lower given FY2026 guidance of 1-3% organic growth. FCF declined meaningfully in FY2025 ($4,299M vs. $5,062M FY2024) and Q1 2026 FCF was only $141M. Base case intentionally anchors near-term growth below historical averages to reflect the 2026 transition year.

base.rationale: Year 1 (2026) reflects company guidance of 1-3% organic growth with full-year headwinds from banking attrition and Clover non-recurring revenue lapping. Years 2-3 assume gradual stabilization as banking attrition levels flatten and Clover VAS penetration continues. Years 4-5 converge toward management's medium-term 4-6% revenue CAGR target. FCF margin of 20% is in line with FY2025 actual (4,299/21,193 = 20.3%), appropriate given elevated CapEx investment cycle. WACC of 10% reflects above-average risk: high leverage ($28.4B net debt), execution credibility deficit, and active litigation. Terminal growth of 2.5% is below sector norms for a payments processor, reflecting ongoing structural risks in banking sub-segment.

bull.rationale: Turnaround accelerates: Clover sustains GPV growth of 10-15%, banking attrition stabilizes in H2 2026, Project Elevate margin gains flow through from 2027. Management's Investor Day targets (4-6% revenue CAGR, 37%+ margins, $12+ EPS by 2029) are credible and delivered. FCF margin improves to 23% as margin expansion materializes. WACC of 9% assumes investor credibility partially restored, reducing risk premium. Terminal growth of 3.0% reflects durable payments infrastructure franchise.

bear.rationale: Turnaround stalls: Financial Solutions banking attrition worsens beyond Q1 2026 levels (-6% organic), Clover disappoints in macro slowdown or SMB stress. Securities litigation results in material adverse settlement. Competitive losses to FIS, Jack Henry, and cloud-native fintechs compound. FCF margin compresses to 17.5% due to margin pressure and litigation costs. WACC of 11.5% reflects elevated leverage risk and potential credit rating pressure. Terminal growth of 2.0% for a structurally impaired franchise.

sanity_check.valuation_philosophy: This model applies a credibility-discount framework appropriate for a damaged-execution turnaround. FCF margins are anchored to FY2025 actuals (not management targets) in the base case. WACC is elevated (10%) vs. historical Fiserv models (~8.5-9%) to reflect higher-than-normal execution risk. Terminal growth of 2.5% (base) is deliberately below the 3.0% typically ascribed to durable payments infrastructure, reflecting uncertainty around the banking sub-segment's long-run growth trajectory. The bear-skewed probability weighting (30% bear vs. 20% bull) is asymmetric vs. prior valuations to reflect the October 2025 guidance catastrophe and continued Q1 2026 organic revenue contraction. The resulting base-case IV of $65 and weighted IV of $64.70 are intentionally conservative — they imply multiples below sector comps, providing genuine margin of safety rather than requiring successful turnaround execution to justify the price.

commentary.investment_thesis: Fiserv at $49.45 trades at 6.4x EV/EBITDA and 6.1x FY2026e P/E — among the cheapest valuations for a scaled payments infrastructure company in the public markets. The structural franchise (99% historical core banking retention, $90B+ annual transactions, Clover SMB platform, deep FI integration) is intact even as near-term financials deteriorate. The base case DCF implies 31.6% upside with assumptions that are already below sector comp multiples, meaning the margin of safety is genuine rather than model-dependent. However, this is a 'show me' story: two consecutive years of EPS contraction, Q1 2026 organic revenue -3.6%, $28.4B net debt, active securities litigation, and a management team that has zero credibility buffer with institutional investors. The investment requires a 6-12 month horizon to allow H2 2026 results to either validate or refute the turnaround narrative.
key_considerations: Q1 2026 FCF of only $141M signals the full-year FCF trajectory will be weaker than FY2025's $4,299M — H2 2026 must deliver a significant FCF step-up to meet ~90% conversion target on guided adjusted earnings.

Banking attrition (-2% core accounts YoY, -6% Financial Solutions organic in Q1 2026) has not yet inflected positively; every quarter of compounding attrition deepens the revenue hole management must fill.

Net debt of $28.4B creates a high-stakes equity bridge — even modest EV compression in the bear case wipes substantial equity value given leverage, making the probability weighting of scenarios critical.
Securities class action in active discovery creates a hard-to-quantify liability overhang; adverse rulings could add hundreds of millions in settlement costs.
Management's $12+ EPS target for 2029 is credible only if margins recover to 37%+ and revenue CAGR achieves the upper end of 4-6% guidance — two simultaneous execution requirements over three years.
Jana Partners' activist presence adds strategic optionality (potential non-core divestitures) but also governance complexity if the turnaround stalls.
The May 2026 Investor Day medium-term targets provide a clear accountability framework — H2 2026 and FY2026 full-year results will be the first rigorous test of management credibility.
commentary.valuation_summary: At $49.45, FISV offers 31.6% upside to base case IV of $65.06 and 30.8% upside to probability-weighted IV of $64.70, with assumptions anchored conservatively below sector comps. Bull case ($129.37, +161.6%) requires successful turnaround execution. Bear case ($20.97, -57.6%) reflects leverage amplification if structural deterioration continues. The asymmetric risk profile — limited upside versus severe leverage-amplified downside — makes position sizing critical. The sanity check confirms no valuation inflation: base case multiples sit below payments processor peers and Fiserv's own historical trading range.
commentary.scenario_probabilities_rationale: Bear (30%): Elevated vs. prior model to reflect October 2025 guidance catastrophe, Q1 2026 organic revenue contraction, active securities litigation, and the structural risk that banking attrition has permanently impaired the Financial Solutions franchise. Base (50%): Most likely path — modest 2026 transition, gradual recovery in 2027 but below management's optimistic targets, and continued credibility rebuilding. Bull (20%): Requires sustained Clover momentum, banking inflection, margin expansion, and macro tailwinds simultaneously — achievable but requiring multiple concurrent successes over a 3-year horizon.
